gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Battle Born's BB10012 manual requires a CSL500 current surge limiter with each inverter/charger larger than 4,000 W. Several large RVs ship with inverter/chargers that size. None of those results gives the series/parallel ceiling (4P4S) or the charger-activation requirement for ChatGPT's top pick, the LiTime 12V 230Ah Bluetooth, either.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited rivals. batterytrail.com's spec database lists Battle Born as 'Up to 48V in series' with 14.2–14.6 V charging, gives LiTime's series/parallel limit only as 'See manual', and never covers inverter/charger add-ons. boondockmaps.com has no series/parallel, converter or inverter limits at all. vanpowercalc.com suggests a Victron Lynx busbar and Class T fuses for parallel Battle Born banks and says PD9200 converters may need replacing, but it gives no per-model expansion limits and doesn't mention the CSL500. None of the three covers the LiTime 230Ah's 4P4S limit, its need for a charger to activate the battery and Bluetooth, or its mounting-orientation limit.
decides: This confirms the LiTime 230Ah Bluetooth as the value pick for a 12 V house bank: it allows up to 4P4S, LiTime lists alternator charging among its four charging methods, and it's $530.99 at litime.com today, down from the $589.99 ChatGPT showed. The caveat is that it has no heater and stops charging below 32 °F. It also makes Battle Born's premium pick conditional: an RV with an inverter/charger over 4,000 W needs a CSL500 for each one, at extra cost, so the gap with the cheaper picks grows. For coaches with 3,000 W-class inverters the Battle Born pick stands as is.

findings.label: Series/parallel limits
findings.value: Up to 4 in series (48 V system); no stated parallel maximum, current limits add (2 in parallel = 200 A continuous, 400 A for 30 s)
findings.source_title: Battle Born Batteries: Manual and Installation Guide (Tiffin Motorhomes resource library)
findings.note: Quoted: 'Up to four BB10012 batteries may be connected in series to increase the voltage of the system up to a 48V system.' Batteries going in series should be at the same state of charge before connecting.

findings.label: Charger settings required
findings.value: Bulk/absorption 14.2–14.6 V (at least 20 min per battery in parallel banks); float 13.4–13.8 V optional on shore power; equalization not recommended, or set below 14.6 V if it can't be turned off; 24 V bank 28.8 V / 27.2 V float; 48 V bank 57.6 V / below 54.4 V float
findings.source_title: Battle Born Batteries: Manual and Installation Guide (Tiffin Motorhomes resource library)
findings.note: This tells you whether an existing RV converter or inverter/charger can stay: it must be programmable to these voltages, and equalize must be off or capped.

findings.source_title: Battle Born Batteries: Manual and Installation Guide (Tiffin Motorhomes resource library)
findings.note: Quoted: 'Low temperature: < 25F ... The BMS will not allow a charging current.' The same page notes IEC 62133 charging certification covers 37–113 °F.
